idiom_name: one mapper (class or function set) per (domain type, message type) pair, invoked by the producing/consuming endpoint
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: keep both representations ignorant of each other; declare one mapper per pair and give every rule a home there - which domain objects contribute, how references flatten to ids, units, time stamps, absent-versus-default and what is deliberately dropped. Keep the wire encoding outside the mapper: the mapper produces or consumes a message value and the endpoint hands that value to the channel or to the serialiser. Write both directions as separate named operations, because their policies differ, and invoke them from one deliberate place - the producer before send, the consumer before domain code - never from the representations themselves. Where the language can declare or generate the mapping (serializer attributes, codecs, generated mappers), let it own the mechanical field copying and keep hand-written code for the conversions with real semantics.
pitfalls: Letting either representation call the mapper itself (to_message methods on the aggregate) recreates the coupling the pattern removes.
Mapping that renames fields but ignores semantics - units, time zones, unknown enum values, absent versus default - produces plausible wrong data.
No policy for unknown and newly added fields: one direction drops them silently and the other invents defaults.
A mapper that grows validation or business rules becomes a shadow domain model nobody owns.

Wrong move: expose an ORM or persistence entity as the message contract -> schema changes, lazy associations and internal fields leak into a public payload -> instead map to a dedicated versioned message type with explicit fields.

Wrong move: let inbound mapping query repositories or enforce business policy -> the mapper becomes nondeterministic shadow domain logic -> instead pass resolved references or context in and keep I/O and invariants in the endpoint or domain service.

Wrong move: treat absent fields and unknown versions as harmless defaults -> rolling upgrades silently change meaning -> instead define per-field compatibility rules and fail or quarantine unsupported required data.
